newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Netanyahu says threats against him.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Netanyahu says threats against him.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Saturday that he had received threats against him but did not elaborate.
Asked about recent threats by ultra-orthodox Jews against Israel's High Court Chief Justice Aharon Barak, Netanyahu told Israel army radio: "There are also threats against me."
An article published last month in an ultra-orthodox newspaper branded Barak a "dangerous enemy" of devout Jews and said God would help religious Jews overcome him.

The article, which blasted Barak over a High Court decision to keep open on the Jewish sabbath a Jerusalem street that runs through an ultra-orthodox neighbourhood, shocked Israelis still recovering from the assassination of their prime minister.
Yitzhak Rabin was shot dead at a peace rally last November by a right-wing Jew opposed to his peace policies.
Asked if the threats were made by members of the left-wing, Netanyahu said: "It is meaningless where they are coming from, whether it's from the left or from the right.
"Death threats or any kind of threats are illegitimate and should be condemned...they are a danger and a crime."
Earlier this month Netanyahu, in what many of his backers felt was a betrayal, met for the first time since taking office in June with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.
After the landmark meeting Leah Rabin, wife of the slain prime minister warned Netanyahu to heed threats against him.
